sections.summary: Defines @cairn/contract/js, an Effect-free entry of parse, format, append and migrate functions plus shipped types and JSON Schemas.
sections.title: JavaScript entry

sections.summary: Defines a deep link in `packages/contract/src/link.ts`: a link is a list of typed steps, and its text is a URL path. One Effect Schema, `LinkFromPath`, turns paths into steps and steps back into paths, enforces the ordering rules, and reports failures as a `LinkError`.
sections.title: Links

sections.summary: Lets PRD and spec list items carry section-style IDs and adds done-when statement IDs (`StatementId`, `ownerOf`), then extends the trace, the commit trailer and the spec index to record items, statements, the tests that prove them and the tasks that trace them, while older files still decode.
sections.title: Items and statements

sections.summary: Declares the eight relation kinds (needs, builtOn, orderedAfter, builds, names, implements, dependsOn, proves) in one typed table in `relations.ts`, with their allowed end kinds and where each is recorded. It also adds the `orderedAfter` field to manifest tasks, which defaults to an empty list.
sections.title: Relation kinds

sections.summary: Extends the contract's `Event` into a union discriminated by `kind` (status, usage, conflict), so that the orchestrator's events record each attempt's harness, token usage, cost, billing route and failure reason. It also adds the derived `Attempt` type that the trace carries.
sections.title: Attempts

sections.summary: Extends the Trace contract with per-task attempts, a terminal flag and usage (per-session token counts, API-equivalent estimates, billed cost, allowance shares and a private allocation), plus private account-wide allowance data, and says which consumers see the private fields.
sections.title: Usage in the trace

sections.summary: Groups the section parsing and cairn ids specs.
sections.title: Sections

sections.summary: sectionsOf(markdown) returns every heading outside a fence as a Section with id, level, title, line, parent, body, human flag and keys.
sections.title: Parsing

sections.summary: cairn ids assigns missing section IDs in prd.md and spec.md, with a --check mode.
sections.title: `cairn ids`

sections.summary: Builds `itemsOf`, a pure function that lists every unfenced list item in a markdown document with its ID, text, line, section, parent and human flag, and `assignItemIds`, which `cairn ids` runs to fill each `{#}` on a list item with an ID made from its heading's ID and its first two words.
sections.title: List items

sections.summary: Makes PRD items with IDs first-class units: defines when an item is covered, adds the `unmapped-item` lint rule and extends existing rules to items, rolls tasks and status up per item and into headings, tags human items in gates, tells the planner prompts to name items, and fills items in the trace.
sections.title: Item coverage

sections.summary: Groups the gate path matching and detection specs.
sections.title: Gates

sections.summary: Gate path patterns use Node path.matchesGlob plus a gitignore rule for slash-less patterns and directory paths. The current directory probe misses suffix and nested-path patterns; t18 is failed pending correction, with existing commits retained.
sections.title: Path matching

sections.summary: gateOf returns whether a task needs a human gate and the reasons, from tags and path patterns, and status derivation recomputes it after commits.
sections.title: Detection

sections.summary: Defines the two model services. LanguageModel comes from a planner source: the person's agent CLI by default, so planning runs on a subscription, or an API provider with a key. DecisionModel is TypeSafe Jev for the Judge, pinned to a version. Claude CLI, Codex CLI and Anthropic API are implemented, and the other API providers are pending. planner.gatewayTokenEnv sends a Cloudflare AI Gateway token with every api request.
sections.title: Models

sections.summary: Groups the planner service, stack order and cairn plan specs.
sections.title: Planning

sections.summary: The Planner service makes six model calls (spec, sections, tasks, splitSection, splitTask, index), each decoded through its schema with one retry, checks that every Mermaid block it returns draws, and never decides gates, IDs, branches, order or the stack diagram.
sections.title: Planner service

sections.summary: stackOf orders drafts by dependency and returns a set of stacks: parentOf puts a task on the latest of its dependencies when they share one chain, and starts it from baseBranch after they land when they do not.
sections.title: Stack order

sections.summary: cairn plan runs two steps with a review after each: it writes the spec and asks before drafting tasks, then drafts, judges, orders and lints the tasks and asks before writing manifest.json. A second run continues from the files on disk.
sections.title: `cairn plan`

sections.summary: replanOf finds what a second cairn plan adds: spec for uncovered PRD sections, tasks for spec sections without one, and reports of what went stale. Existing tasks are never changed.
sections.title: Planning again

sections.summary: stackDiagramOf draws the plan's stacks as Mermaid from manifest.json, and withStackDiagram writes it between markers in spec.md on every manifest write. The stack grouping moves to core and the viewer imports it.
sections.title: Stack diagram

sections.summary: cairn plan --dry-run plans in memory, writes nothing and prints a totals line; --source, --provider and --model replace the config's planner for one run so two planners can be compared.
sections.title: Dry runs

sections.summary: This section covers how Cairn carries PRD done-when statements through a build. Each statement is parsed and given an ID, drafts are reviewed with the person, the planner writes a test for each statement, statements are attached to tasks in spec.json and the trace, and they are shown in the agent's brief, cairn status, gates and the viewer.
sections.title: Done when

sections.summary: Defines how done-when statements are read from PRD markdown (`statementsOf`), given stable owner-scoped IDs (`assignStatementIds`, run by `cairn ids`), and checked by a new `statement-owner` lint error.
sections.title: Statements

sections.summary: Adds a `statements` call to the Planner that drafts "Done when" statements for PRD sections and items that have none, pure core functions to insert drafts (`withDrafts`) and settle answers (`settle`), and an `ask-statements.ts` step in `cairn plan` that asks the person to accept, rewrite, delete or skip each draft before the spec step.
sections.title: Asking the person

sections.summary: Makes the planner trace tests to PRD statements: prompts make each test end with the statement IDs it proves, `Planner.index` fills and checks each test's `proves`, a pure `taskStatementsOf` works out which statements a task carries and which tests prove them, and three lint warnings flag draft statements, unproved statements and tasks with no statement.
sections.title: Tracing statements

sections.summary: Adds `formatStatements` to `@cairn/contract/js`, which renders a task's done-when statements as a markdown "Done when:" block. The block goes at the top of agent briefs, into `cairn status --task` and `cairn approve` (as a review checklist), and into the viewer's task detail.
sections.title: Statements in briefs and reviews

sections.summary: Adds a category to planned tasks: a configurable list of categories in the config, a required category on task drafts and an optional one on manifest tasks, prompt and decode checks against the list, and two lint rules for unknown and missing categories.
sections.title: Task categories

sections.summary: Defines how Cairn predicts merge conflicts between tasks that can run in parallel: it reads git history for file churn and co-change, then scores each parallel pair of tasks from the files they share, couple, or touch additively or as generated output, with configurable patterns and thresholds.
sections.title: Conflict scores

sections.summary: Builds `orderingsOf`, which takes high-scoring conflict pairs among new drafts and either stacks the later task on the earlier one through `orderedAfter` or records a recommendation. It also covers the lint rules, the plan output, `undo <n>` and the `splitFile` judgment that go with it.
sections.title: Conflict ordering

sections.summary: Adds `cairn plan <id>...`, which plans one part of the PRD: the named headings and list items plus everything under them. It refuses unknown IDs without touching `.cairn/`, narrows the replan scope, planner checks, done-when questions, judging and lint blocking to that part, and keeps reporting staleness and unplanned sections over the whole plan.
sections.title: Planning a part

sections.summary: lint is a pure function returning findings for eleven rules, printed by a command that exits 1 on any error.
sections.title: Lint

sections.summary: Judging asks a decision model at each step of the breakdown whether pieces are the right size and which model each task needs; the language model writes and splits, and code keeps every change within bounds.
sections.title: Judging

sections.summary: Three Decision.make definitions in core, for spec sections, tasks and the stack, and a pure inputsOf; tasks are asked size, matches, model and reasoning.
sections.title: Questions

sections.summary: verdictOf turns judging answers into pass, flag or unsure, and routeOf picks the model and reasoning, using Jev only when it is confident.
sections.title: Verdicts

sections.summary: The Judge hashes each input, keeps unchanged judgments without a call, and asks the rest through DecisionModel.decideSettled, four requests at a time, with typed errors and rate-limit retries.
sections.title: Judge service

sections.summary: refine runs the section, task-size and routing checkpoints, splitting confidently oversized pieces through the Planner within judge.maxRounds and recording every change as a judgment.
sections.title: Checkpoints

sections.summary: cairn judge judges the current spec and manifest, writes judgments.json and prints flag and unsure lines; --fresh asks again and --strict exits 1 on a flag.
sections.title: `cairn judge`

sections.summary: Adds a model catalog and the person's access, harnesses and preferences to routing config, pure catalog functions for eligibility and pricing, and a routing question that recommends a model and reasoning setting per task by expected total cost. Recommendations are recorded on judgments, applied only when the provider is validated, shown in plan output, and can be overridden per task with `set`.
sections.title: Model catalog

sections.summary: Adds a second DecisionModel Layer that calls the OpenAI Decisions API over HttpClient, with its own config block, thresholds and routing switch. It also maps OpenAI's answer types onto Judgment answers, including a new ScoreAnswer and a scoreKind on RateAnswer, and records the provider and pinned model per judgment.
sections.title: OpenAI Decisions

sections.summary: Adds `cairn judge --compare --tasks <ids>`, which asks both decision providers the task questions for person-chosen tasks, records each request in a new `evaluations` table in `cairn.db`, and prints per-task answers beside the manifest's assignments plus agreement, latency, token and cost totals. A dollar and request budget limits the run.
sections.title: Comparing decision providers

sections.summary: Routes Cairn's API calls (API-sourced planner and the OpenAI Decisions judge) through Cloudflare AI Gateway by default, with a required `gateway` config block covering account, token, billing mode and request logging, explicit `route` keys, secret redaction, and error handling for a gateway that does not serve the Decisions endpoint.
sections.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway

sections.summary: Builds history-based model routing: a pure `rankOf` that ranks eligible (model, reasoning, harness) candidates per task category by cost per verified task from recent outcomes, and wires its recommendation into `refine` at the routing checkpoint as a `history` judgment, with opt-in adaptive application and deterministic exploration.
sections.title: Routing from history

sections.summary: Groups the task machine, derivation, section rollup and cairn status/approve specs.
sections.title: Status

sections.summary: The task machine gains a failed state, keeps the gate, and lands from any status but landed.
sections.title: Task machine

sections.summary: derive recomputes every task status from manifest, events and commits by folding events through the task machine and landing from git whatever the status, with warnings for anything ignored.
sections.title: Derivation

sections.summary: A section's status is rolled up from its linked tasks and descendants by an ordered first-match rule list.
sections.title: Section rollup

sections.summary: cairn status prints the stack and warnings; cairn approve records a human approval; Git.log reads task branches.
sections.title: `cairn status` and `cairn approve`

sections.summary: A commit-msg hook refuses a commit on a task branch without its Cairn-Task and Cairn-Section trailers, so every task commit can land.
sections.title: Trailer check

sections.summary: Builds `attemptsOf`, a pure function that splits each task's status events into attempts with a kind, an outcome and a cost. It also adds per-task attempt and cost limits that make a task terminal, `taskCostOf` for summing a task's cost, and a `usage_reports` table that stores raw provider usage reports.
sections.title: Attempts

sections.summary: Defines the pure function `metricsOf`, which groups finished tasks by any combination of category, model, reasoning and harness and computes outcome metrics for each group, such as cost per verified task, first-pass rate, time to done, failure rates and cache use. Tasks with unknown cost are counted in `leftOut` and never treated as free.
sections.title: Outcome metrics

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn stats` command, which derives attempts from `events.jsonl` and prints per-category outcome metrics tables (one row per model, reasoning level and harness), followed by routed tasks and, in shadow mode, a comparison of history recommendations with what ran. It supports `--category`, `--since` and `--json` and is read-only and local.
sections.title: `cairn stats`

sections.summary: Builds the relation index: a pure `indexOf(source)` that extracts typed relations from the manifest, spec index and PRD (or from a trace) and answers graph queries over them, such as what points where, build order, which tasks can start, what waits on what, dangling ends and cycles.
sections.title: Relation index

sections.summary: Builds `sectionLinksOf`, a pure function that, for a PRD section or an ID'd list item, reports which other sections or items it needs and is needed by through task dependencies, and lists its unfinished tasks in build order, with a transitive mode as well.
sections.title: Section links

sections.summary: Makes the relation index the single source for what a task needs or waits on: lint gains a `need-cycle` error, the trace and `cairn status` report whether each task can start and what it waits on, stack layout reads from the index, and the viewer builds the same index from the trace.
sections.title: Answers from the index

sections.summary: Treats the restack conflict events already in `events.jsonl` as the conflict record, adds a pure `calibrationOf` function that counts restacks and conflicts among high- and low-scoring pairs, and has `cairn status` end with a one-line summary of those counts.
sections.title: Conflict record

sections.summary: Groups the specification of session storage, redaction and the session command.
sections.title: Sessions

sections.summary: Specifies the SQLite trace store for redacted sessions, on Effect SQL's SqliteClient with Effect migrations; notes wait for their own migration.
sections.title: Trace store

sections.summary: Specifies redact(jsonl, secrets), which rewrites every decoded string value in a session log, its secret sources and fail-closed behaviour.
sections.title: Redaction

sections.summary: Specifies the `cairn session put` command, which redacts and stores a session log.
sections.title: `cairn session`

sections.summary: sessionOf(log, stored) in core reads a redacted Claude Code JSONL log into a Session, decoding only the fields it uses and taking file edits from toolUseResult.
sections.title: Reading a session

sections.summary: Reads Codex rollouts into per-call usage records (codexUsageOf), stores them idempotently in a new usage_calls table alongside session allocations and subagent links, and computes each task's usage total over distinct, share-weighted sessions (taskUsageOf), surfaced on TraceTask.usage.
sections.title: Usage records

sections.summary: Builds the pure function `estimateOf(calls, catalog)`. It prices each call in a session from the model catalog and returns an `Estimate`, labelled API-equivalent cost. The estimate is deterministic, works in integer micro-dollars, tracks which calls were priced, and records its rate sources, assumptions and excluded charges.
sections.title: API-equivalent cost

sections.summary: Builds subscription accounting for sessions billed on a plan rather than per token. It stores Codex rate-limit snapshots and turns them into account use and per-session allowance consumption with `allowanceOf`. It also spreads a configured subscription fee across sessions with `allocationOf`. Billed cost stays `null` throughout.
sections.title: Subscription allowance

sections.summary: Adds notes and reviews anchored to link paths: a Note type and `notes` table, `cairn note add` and `cairn note resolve` commands, and server support that reads notes into the trace and attaches them to their sessions.
sections.title: Notes

sections.summary: Lists what the existing orchestrator must do per task using only @cairn/contract/js and the CLI.
sections.title: Orchestrator adapter

sections.summary: Defines what the orchestrator adds to each task run: attempt metadata on the `running` event, a verify command run in the task's worktree that decides `done`, `blocked_on_human` or `failed` (with a failure kind), usage, cost and route on the final event, and session and usage recording through the cairn CLI. AGENTS.md documents these fields for adapter writers.
sections.title: Attempts and verification

sections.summary: Adds conflict-aware scheduling: a pure `scheduleOf` that orders ready tasks by conflict risk against running tasks, detects overlapping hunks between running tasks, and orders stack landing. It also covers the orchestrator behaviour (hold/release/notice/restack events, notices to agents, restacking on land) and how conflict events show in `cairn status` and the viewer timeline.
sections.title: Conflict-aware running

sections.summary: Specifies the single cairn binary built with effect/cli and the cairn init command.
sections.title: CLI

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn link` command, which turns ordered command-line tokens into viewer steps, checks them against the PRD, spec, manifest and git, and prints a viewer deep link encoded with `LinkFromPath`. It also sets the rule that agents and the orchestrator name places in PRs, gate notices and board posts with `cairn link`.
sections.title: `cairn link`

sections.summary: Builds the Cairn docs site, served under /docs/ on prdtrace.com beside the demo, for people setting Cairn up and for agents working in a repo. Its reference pages are generated from the code and it shows the real viewer.
sections.title: Documentation

sections.summary: Builds a build-time generator that writes the CLI reference pages from the `effect/cli` command definitions and the `.cairn/` file pages from the contract's generated JSON Schema. It also adds a check that fails the build when a docs page names a `cairn` command that no longer exists.
sections.title: Reference from code

sections.summary: Builds `apps/docs`, a Foldkit docs app. Its markdown pages render through the viewer's markdown renderer, it has sidebar navigation, and its search index is ranked by the viewer's matcher. Pages are prerendered to static HTML and deployed by `apps/site` under `/docs/`.
sections.title: Docs site

sections.summary: Builds the hand-written markdown pages of the documentation site: getting started, section IDs and done-when statements, planning, judging, human gates, cost per verified task, conflict-aware ordering, writing an orchestrator adapter, and the viewer with deep links.
sections.title: Pages

sections.summary: Lets a docs page embed the live demo viewer: a fenced `cairn-viewer` block holding a link path is rendered as a 640px-high iframe of the demo viewer at that path, showing this repo's own plan.
sections.title: The viewer on a page

sections.summary: Builds agent access to Cairn: the CLI and a stdio MCP server (`cairn mcp`) as thin adapters over one shared operation layer in `packages/cli/src/operations/`, with schemas in `@cairn/contract`. Planning's questions and reviews become resumable decisions, and the work includes a guide and setup instructions.
sections.title: Agent access

sections.summary: Declares Cairn's operations as data in the contract package (Operation, OperationError, Finding, humanOnly) and adds the init, ids, lint and status operations. Both adapters run them through a single runOperation entry point. Writes are atomic and recorded, an operations table logs each run so interrupted runs are reported, and an equivalence test checks that the CLI and JSON paths give the same results.
sections.title: Operations

sections.summary: Turns `cairn plan` into a `plan` operation that stops at each review question (statements, spec, tasks) and returns it as a stored, revision-guarded decision, plus a `plan-continue` operation that applies the answer. The interactive CLI and new `--json` and `--continue` flags drive the same two operations.
sections.title: Review checkpoints

sections.summary: Builds `cairn mcp`, an MCP server over stdio bound to one repository, which advertises Cairn's existing operations as tools from a registry, runs calls through `runOperation` with progress and cancellation, and keeps stdout for protocol messages only. It also adds an MCP leg to the equivalence harness and end-to-end, cancellation and shutdown tests.
sections.title: MCP server

sections.summary: Adds an operation and a matching MCP tool for `judge`, `stats`, `link`, `note add`, `note resolve` and starting and stopping `serve`, each a small adapter over the existing operation layer. It also says which commands get no tool.
sections.title: More tools

sections.summary: Writes the agent guide: a short `SKILL.md` shipped with the CLI package and a matching docs page, `10-agents.md`. Together they cover the workflow, the human checkpoints, how to recover from each error, the limits and MCP setup. The page also includes a tools table that `reference.ts` generates from the registry.
sections.title: Agent guide

sections.summary: Builds `cairn watch`, a read-only terminal viewer that follows `.cairn/` and git, rebuilds the trace into a Model and draws it with a pure `view` into a Frame. The section covers the refresh pipeline and the screen layout: a top status line, a task tree pane, a detail pane for the selected task and a key-hint line.
sections.title: Terminal view

sections.summary: Builds the CLI watch view's rendering layer: a spike that tests OpenTUI's core against four requirements, a pure in-memory Frame model in frame.ts, and a Screen service with a memory implementation for tests and a diffing ANSI implementation. The ANSI screen has no dependencies and is the fallback if the spike fails.
sections.title: Rendering library

sections.summary: Moves the derivations of status counts, status tree order and what ran into `core`, so that `cairn status` and the viewer share one implementation: `statusTreeOf`, `statusCountsOf` and `ranOf`.
sections.title: Shared derivations

sections.summary: Builds `traceStream(root)`, a scoped stream that watches `.cairn/` and git refs and also polls. After a debounce it rebuilds the trace through the same `buildTrace` the `/api/trace` route uses, but only when the input hash has changed.
sections.title: Trace stream

sections.summary: Builds the terminal watch view in the same shape as the viewer: a Schema-defined WatchModel, fact-named Messages, a single `update` returning commands and a single `view` producing a Frame, plus a symbol table for statuses in Unicode and ASCII. It also sets out the memory, selection, tick and layout rules, and the tests for them.
sections.title: Model, update and view

sections.summary: Defines the terminal view's key handling: the `Key` type, a pure `keysFor(model)` that lists the keys that apply now (drawn on the bottom line), and how `update` acts on each key. That covers navigation, opening a task, text and status filtering, help, opening the task in the viewer and quitting.
sections.title: Keys

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn watch` command: it refuses to run without a terminal, otherwise sets up colour/Unicode detection, raw mode, the alternate screen, listeners, signal handlers, the trace stream and a tick inside one Effect Scope, runs the update/view loop, and restores the terminal on every exit path. It runs on a read-only FileSystem, so it cannot affect the run it watches.
sections.title: `cairn watch`

sections.summary: Builds the read-only `cairn doctor` command, which runs three checks in order (git, config, planner), prints one plain `ok`/`fail` line per check saying what to fix, and exits 0 only when every check passes.
sections.title: `cairn doctor`

sections.summary: Two git-backed routes on the dev server, GET /api/commits/:sha and GET /api/diffs/:base/:head, return a commit's patch and a task's whole diff as text for the code view.
sections.title: Patch routes

sections.summary: Specifies the cairn serve HTTP and WebSocket routes on port 4310 and how the viewer polls them.
sections.title: Server

sections.summary: Groups the viewer specification.
sections.title: Viewer

sections.summary: Specifies the viewer model, the messages every screen shares, the pure chainOf function, hovering a chain, and the three-pane layout.
sections.title: Model and messages

sections.summary: Specifies how the viewer renders markdown to Foldkit nodes without innerHTML.
sections.title: Markdown rendering

sections.summary: Specifies the viewer's design tokens for a light and a dark palette, its three stylesheets, the classes and controls every view is built from, and the move of the code view to them.
sections.title: Design system

sections.summary: Specifies the reader screen: the PRD read as a document in its own pane, with a status line under each heading, and the section at the top of the pane, or the pinned one, as the current section the other panes follow.
sections.title: Reader

sections.summary: Specifies the spec pane: one card per spec section that implements the current PRD section, with its summary, its tasks as rows inside it, and one control for how much of every card shows.
sections.title: Spec cards

sections.summary: Index and rank fuzzy matches for titles, IDs and branches.
sections.title: Fuzzy matching

sections.summary: Add search navigation and temporary chain highlighting.
sections.title: Search controls and chain highlighting

sections.summary: Search markdown prose with snippets and inline match highlights.
sections.title: Prose search and inline highlights

sections.summary: Specifies the curves that join the three panes for the current section: pure links and paths from measured rectangles, held inside their panes, measured by one Mount and lit along a chain on hover.
sections.title: Curves

sections.summary: Lays the stacks pane out like the spec's stack diagram: one numbered box per stack, a chip per task bottom to top inside it, and the boxes in rows over the base branch by what they wait on, with the current section's tasks standing out.
sections.title: Stacks

sections.summary: Defines the pure `boxOf` function that works out what a stack's box draws before it is drawn: depth-first columns, spans centred over forks, a finished trunk that folds into a segment, fork labels from spec sections, and the keys parent arrows run between. It also defines the trunk's label text.
sections.title: Boxes, forks and finished trunks

sections.summary: Draws a stack's box as a grid of chip rows and gap rows, with fork labels under labelled children and a segment button that folds and unfolds the box's trunk. Folded tasks are found through their segment by links, curves and scrolls, and fold state lives only in the window.
sections.title: Drawing a box

sections.summary: Draws parent arrows between the chips, fork labels and segments of the stacks list: a pure `arrowsOf` computes each arrow's end points and bezier path from the rectangles `MeasureWires` already measures, and `arrowsView` renders them as an SVG overlay under the chips.
sections.title: Parent arrows

sections.summary: Draws dashed dependency arrows between a focused task (hovered, keyboard-focused or open in the detail panel) and the tasks in other stacks it depends on or that depend on it, and lights the tasks at the other ends.
sections.title: Dependency arrows

sections.summary: Specifies how the reader shows the model and reasoning each task ran with, or the plan's choice when it has not run, and the switch that shows or hides them everywhere.
sections.title: Models and reasoning

sections.summary: Specifies the dividers that resize the PRD pane, the spec pane and the detail panel by pointer or arrow keys, within limits, with the stacks pane taking what is left.
sections.title: Panes

sections.summary: Presence says which PRD section each participant is reading, shown as a chip beside that heading; pointer cursors stay on the canvas until it is removed, since no two reader windows could place one alike.
sections.title: Presence in the reader

sections.summary: Specifies the detail panel over the right of the reader: a trail of nodes, and for a task its status, what ran, its parent and dependencies, gate reasons, code, commits, traces and timeline.
sections.title: Detail panel

sections.summary: The code view screen: a stack tree, the selected task's whole diff or one commit's diff, and the session pane, opened from the detail panel and left with Back to the plan.
sections.title: Code view

sections.summary: Renders a task's whole diff or one commit's diff with @pierre/diffs: parsePatchFiles into FileDiffMetadata, one vanilla CodeView in a Foldkit Mount, syntax-highlighted through the Highlights backend.
sections.title: Diff view

sections.summary: The session pane draws the selected commit's session: notes and redaction counts, prompts and replies as markdown, and each tool call as one line that opens.
sections.title: Session pane

sections.summary: attributionOf(files, session) traces each hunk's changed lines to the last tool turn whose edit wrote them, and the diff and session pane link through those marks.
sections.title: Hunks and turns

sections.summary: Specifies the code and the agent session inside a task's detail: its whole stacked diff in the code view's mount, and the first prompt and tool calls of its latest commit's session.
sections.title: Code in the detail panel

sections.summary: Makes the reader the only plan screen and deletes the canvas with everything only it uses, after a human approves the loss of pan and zoom, dragging, coloured pins and pointer cursors.
sections.title: Replacing the canvas

sections.summary: Specifies the demo: a Trace generated from this repo's own .cairn/, what ran on its running events, and the commit patches its build ships as static files so the demo shows code without a server.
sections.title: Demo data

sections.summary: Every place the reader and the code view can open gets a deep link written with `LinkFromPath`. The section covers resolving a link against the trace and loaded data, opening it with the address bar and history kept in sync, and a "Copy link" action on every step. The canvas screen has no links.
sections.title: Deep links

sections.summary: Defines the pure `resolveLink` function that checks a deep link's steps in order against the trace and loaded data. It returns what opened, what is still waiting for data and what is missing. It also defines the `linkNoticeView` status notice that tells the reader how far a link opened and why it stopped.
sections.title: Resolving a link

sections.summary: Makes the viewer a Foldkit application that owns the URL: a single `linkRoute`, `linkOf` to derive the canonical link from the model, `openLink` to apply a link's steps the way clicks would, and `withAddress` to keep browser history in step so Back walks a link one step at a time.
sections.title: Opening a link

sections.summary: Adds copy-link buttons across the viewer (PRD headings, spec cards, passages, the detail trail, stack boxes, the code view, diff lines and session turns). The buttons copy the same deep link the address bar holds, or a shorter link that opens one step on its own. The section also defines the pure `aloneOf` function in `links.ts`, which builds that shortest link.
sections.title: Copying a link

sections.summary: Makes list items that carry an ID behave in the viewer like small sections inside their section. Each such item gets a coverage annotation and a copyable ID. Items can be hovered, pinned and linked from spec cards and task rows, and their coverage counts toward the section's own counts.
sections.title: List items

sections.summary: Adds API-equivalent cost estimates and allowance usage to the viewer: pure helpers in cost.ts (compactOf, cardCostOf, allowanceOf) and their display in the detail panel, task rows and card headers. It also covers narrow-width and keyboard behaviour.
sections.title: Cost on the graph

sections.summary: Adds an attempts list to the task detail panel, below the cost block, with one row per attempt, a line for a task that stopped at its attempt limit, and under the list the routing decision that chose the task's model, taken from the trace's `model` and `history` judgments.
sections.title: Attempts in the detail panel

sections.summary: Adds dependency links to the viewer: each heading and item shows how many sections it needs and how many need it, plus how many of its tasks are ready. A links button opens a list under the heading of what it needs, what needs it, and its next tasks. The task detail panel gains a `Needed by` list and says whether a pending task can start.
sections.title: What depends on what

sections.summary: Builds a ⌘K-style command menu for the viewer in Foldkit: a modal dialog opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K, `/` or the toolbar search button. It lists commands, tasks, and PRD and spec matches ranked by the same fuzzy search index as the toolbar search. It also has nested search pages, keyboard navigation, chain preview and an accessible combobox/listbox view.
sections.title: Command menu

sections.summary: Shows review notes in the viewer: a pure `notesOf` resolves each note's anchor and places it beside a PRD passage or heading, a spec card header, a task row and chip, or a diff line. Notes whose anchors don't fully resolve go into a missing list, and resolved notes are hidden unless a window-local switch is on.
sections.title: Notes

sections.summary: Moves the viewer from Foldkit 0.171.0 to Effect UI in seven steps, each passing `pnpm check`: the Effect upgrade, a gated spike, an Effect UI host over the Foldkit views, the tests, the views top down, removing Foldkit, then components.
sections.title: Effect UI

sections.summary: Moves `effect`, `@effect/vitest` and every `@effect/*` package pinned at 4.1.5 to 4.1.6 in one change and rebuilds the Effect API lookup.
sections.title: Effect 4.1.6

sections.summary: Installs Effect UI from one pinned pkg.pr.new snapshot, rebuilds the switch and disclosure on `@effect/ui-kit`, prototypes a bridge that renders Foldkit views under Effect UI, and writes a report of what Effect UI lacks for a person to read before the port.
sections.title: Spike

sections.summary: Mounts the viewer as one Effect UI component, `Viewer`, whose update wraps today's update and whose view renders today's Foldkit views through the bridge, with the address and subscriptions on Effect UI.
sections.title: The host

sections.summary: Moves every Scene test from `foldkit/scene` to `HtmlScene` on `Viewer` and the Story tests to `Story`, keeping each test's name, clicks and checks.
sections.title: Scene tests

sections.summary: Rewrites the viewer's views in Effect UI's `h` from the top down, in five parts (frame, reader, stacks, detail and code, markdown), with lower views bridged until their part moves.
sections.title: Views

sections.summary: Ports anything left on Foldkit, makes update return Effect UI results itself, deletes the bridge and uninstalls every Foldkit package, its patch and plugins, and points the docs at Effect UI.
sections.title: Removing Foldkit

sections.summary: Splits `Viewer` into pane components (PRD, spec, stacks, task detail and code view) that own their Model and Messages, with shared state in a Provider and pane events mapped in `onEmit`.
sections.title: Components

sections.summary: Groups the model-based tests: the tools, then one model per piece of code tested against it.
sections.title: Testing

sections.summary: Adds @xstate/test on xstate 6.0.0-beta.5 and sets how a model test is written, seeded, covered and replayed.
sections.title: Model-based tests

sections.summary: Tests the presence server over real WebSockets against the room machine, so every participant sees the machine's room.
sections.title: Presence against the room machine

sections.summary: Tests the viewer's update against two machines written from the spec: the detail trail with pinning and Escape, and the pane dividers.
sections.title: Reader interactions against models

sections.summary: Tests derive against a machine of what an orchestrator writes and what git shows, which keeps facts and replays them as derive recomputes.
sections.title: Derivation against a model of its inputs

sections.summary: Maps each PRD acceptance criterion to how it is checked.
sections.title: Acceptance

sections.summary: Builds Cairn's hosted service (launching as prdddd): a single shared Cloudflare application where people sign up into their own workspace, with a Worker in front of D1, one PrdRoom Durable Object per PRD, and R2 for large revision bodies. It brings forward only the parts of the deferred v2 multiplayer architecture that the launch needs.
sections.title: Hosted launch

sections.summary: Defines the shared hosted contract exported from `@cairn/contract/hosted`: ID formats, principals, workspaces, membership and access, documents, revisions, discussion threads, plan records, entitlements, WebSocket room messages and error shapes that the Worker, the viewer and `cairn connect` exchange, plus regenerated JSON Schema files.
sections.title: Hosted contract

sections.summary: Defines the pure `decide(facts, action)` policy function in core, the single authority on whether a person, agent or anonymous reader may perform an action. It covers document access rules, agent ceilings, the per-action allow table, and how the Worker maps a denial to 404 or 403.
sections.title: Policy

sections.summary: Builds `apps/hosted`: a single Cloudflare Worker for every workspace. It uses an Effect HTTP router, resolves each request to a principal, loads facts from D1, and keeps one `PrdRoom` Durable Object per document with its own SQLite. It also covers the D1 schema, R2 storage for large revision bodies, caching headers, the Alchemy deploy and the Workers-pool tests.
sections.title: Worker and storage

sections.summary: Builds sign-in on Better Auth in the Cloudflare Worker, with GitHub, Google, magic-link and device authorization. Sign-up creates a personal workspace for each new user. Workspaces sit on Better Auth's organization plugin. The section also defines a Mailer service and the `GET /api/me` and `POST /api/workspaces` routes.
sections.title: Accounts and workspaces

sections.summary: Builds plan limits for the hosted product: plans decoded from a `PLANS` JSON binding, atomic per-dimension usage reservations that fail with `limit-reached`, an entitlements endpoint for members, and over-limit handling that only blocks new reservations.
sections.title: Entitlements

sections.summary: Builds the per-PRD Durable Object room that linearizes and deduplicates writes, pushes live updates over hibernating WebSockets with a state endpoint for reconnects, and the `revoke` flow that withdraws a member's, guest's or agent's access, closing their open sockets before the request returns.
sections.title: Room

sections.summary: Stores every accepted PRD or spec edit as a numbered, durable revision in the document's room, with save, list, read and restore RPCs, stale-base rejection, and the HTTP routes that expose them to editors and history readers.
sections.title: Revisions

sections.summary: Builds the workspace document directory for hosted Cairn: routes to create, import, list, find, read, rename and export standalone PRDs, each with a stable DocumentId. It also covers the browser address scheme, which keeps working after a rename and gives the same 404 for a document outside the workspace as for an unknown one.
sections.title: Document directory

sections.summary: Builds the hosted API for workspace members and per-document guests: listing members, inviting by email, changing roles, removing members, sharing a single PRD with a guest, and accepting single-use, address-bound invitation tokens. Guests can reach only the documents shared with them and get 404 everywhere else in the workspace.
sections.title: Members and invitations

sections.summary: Builds agent identities with their own revocable, scoped credentials whose access follows their delegating person, the progress-event endpoint that records events with a server-set actor, and person-only gate approvals tied to the PRD, spec and plan revisions current at the time.
sections.title: Agent credentials and gate approvals

sections.summary: Builds whole-PRD public/private visibility for the hosted service: the visibility-change route and its side effects, an FTS5 search table of public documents, server-rendered public pages with SEO metadata, discovery routes (explore, search API, sitemap, robots), and a redacted public view of plan traces, with private documents hidden from every anonymous surface.
sections.title: Visibility

sections.summary: Builds document discussion in the hosted room: durable threads, replies, comment edits and resolution behind policy-checked HTTP routes, plus core's pure `anchorStateOf`, which reports whether a thread's anchor is still attached to the current revision or has changed.
sections.title: Discussion

sections.summary: Adds links between PRDs written as markdown links with a `doc:<DocumentId>[#<SectionId>]` href: core extracts them, the hosted Worker stores them in a `document_links` table on each save and serves access-checked `links` and `backlinks` routes, and the viewer renders resolved links, "No access" chips and a backlinks list.
sections.title: Links between PRDs

sections.summary: Builds the viewer's build-time data source selection: a `__CAIRN_SOURCE__` set from the Vite mode (demo, local or hosted), one loader per source in `load.ts` with no fallback between them, and bundles in which the demo trace appears only in the demo build.
sections.title: Data sources

sections.summary: Builds the hosted viewer's screens around the existing reader: sign-in, workspace switcher, PRD list, empty states, limit notes, the markdown editor with stale-save handling, revision history with restore, and live updates over the document's socket.
sections.title: Workspace screens

sections.summary: Builds the hosted viewer's workspace settings screens: the Members page (members, roles, invitations, removal), the Agents page (listing, creating and revoking agent credentials), and the `/invite/<token>` invitation acceptance page.
sections.title: Workspace settings

sections.summary: Builds the "Share" dialog for a PRD: it explains who can access the document and why, lets managers invite guests and change or remove access, and makes changing visibility to public or private a two-step confirmation that spells out what is exposed or what cannot be recalled.
sections.title: Sharing dialog

sections.summary: Adds comment threads to the reader: starting a thread from a selected passage or a heading, markers on passages and headings with open threads, and a thread node in the detail panel that shows the anchor, comments and policy-allowed actions, kept live by `thread` messages from the room.
sections.title: Comments in the reader

sections.summary: Builds the `cairn connect` CLI commands that link one repo's `.cairn/` directory to one hosted PRD: signing in, storing credentials and agent tokens, and a four-step sync (documents, events, plan, approvals) that never overwrites unsynced local text.
sections.title: `cairn connect`

sections.summary: Records which PRD a plan was made from: `cairn plan` writes the PRD's SHA-256 into the manifest, the hosted room matches it to a PRD revision once when the plan is uploaded, and the viewer warns when the plan or an approval was made against an older PRD revision or an unsynced local draft.
sections.title: Plan source

sections.summary: Bills each workspace through Stripe: a D1 migration for subscriptions and processed webhook events, checkout and customer-portal routes, an idempotent webhook handler that sets subscription state from the latest Stripe object, a mapping from Stripe status to entitlements, and a billing settings screen.
sections.title: Billing

sections.summary: Makes the hosted Worker deployable by an operator in their own Cloudflare account from a settings schema, adds operator backup and restore routes, CLI commands and a weekly restore drill, and writes the hosted, self-hosting, backup and support docs.
sections.title: Self-hosting

sections.summary: Defines the hosted release gates and the tests that check them. It covers two end-to-end acceptance flows in `launch.test.ts`, a cross-workspace isolation property test in `isolation.test.ts`, and a manual staging walkthrough plus a first-time operator self-host run recorded in `checklist.md`.
sections.title: Launch acceptance

sections.summary: Groups the refactors that make the code smaller without changing what it does, each with the pattern it uses and where that came from.
sections.title: Refactors

sections.summary: Adds the Recorder service factory and the shared test fixtures built beside it, and records the pattern in the Effect checklist.
sections.title: Service factories

sections.summary: Asks for the Judge with Effect.serviceOption in cairn plan and provides it only when it is configured, so the provided layer is the only switch for judging.
sections.title: Optional services

sections.summary: Gives each planner call its own Chat so a retry is a follow-up turn carrying only the error, and runs the splits of a refine round as branches of one trunk chat that holds the spec, with chat.ts's branch providing a copy of the current Chat through Effect.provideServiceEffect.
sections.title: Branching conversations

sections.summary: Captures the context an effect stored and run elsewhere takes along without the capturer's Scope, and records where the work still to come takes the pattern.
sections.title: Carrying context

sections.summary: Lets the API routes' failures render their own responses and stay out of error reporting when a caller caused them, and records where the hosted API, its room and the CLI operations take the pattern.
sections.title: Errors that render themselves

sections.summary: Makes the files Cairn writes appear whole or not at all, by staging each beside its target and publishing it with one rename or link, and records where the work still to come takes the pattern.
sections.title: Atomic writes

sections.summary: Declares each record that goes to several places once, with each field saying which of its shapes have it, for the spec index, the task and the sessions table, and records where the work still to come takes the pattern.
sections.title: Variant schemas
